name: S M Automotive Ltd
note: No website anywhere. Of 21 auto shops on the same Calgary directory page, this is the only one without one.
angle: Every competitor in their category already ranks. Show them the directory page with their name as the one blank row.

name: Karmic Book
note: No website. Registered as Karmic Books Inc. and actively hiring oil-and-gas bookkeepers through job boards.
angle: They're recruiting with no site for candidates to look at. Lead with hiring credibility, not marketing.

name: Aman's Barber Shop
note: No website and no social presence found - only Yelp and directory scrapes.
angle: A one-page site with hours, prices and a map beats a Yelp page they don't control.

name: The Supreme Barbershop
note: Instagram plus a bare Cojilio booking link. No website tying them together.
angle: They already pay for booking software. The site just needs to wrap it - cheap to sell, fast to build.

name: Blind Barber
note: No website. The only web property found is a single third-party business listing.
angle: Their name collides with a large US chain in search results - a local site is the only way they surface for Calgary.

name: Bignold Painting
note: Site loads over plain HTTP - the HTTPS address bounces straight back to HTTP, so browsers flag it as not secure. They're also split across two domains, bignold.com and bignoldpainting.com, which divides their search authority.
angle: The 'Not secure' warning in Chrome is a concrete, screenshot-able problem. Consolidate to one domain with a certificate.

name: Balwin Collision Repairs (1984) Ltd
note: Trading since 1984 with no website. Directories and Yelp only.
angle: Four decades of reputation with nothing online carrying it. Insurance-claim work goes to shops customers can vet.

name: Ken-Zee Hair Co
note: Their 'site' is a salonpages.ca template subdomain served over plain HTTP - not their own domain, not their own design.
angle: They already accepted they need a web page. Sell them the upgrade to a domain they own, not the idea of a site.

name: Cristina's Hair Salon Ltd
note: A Fresha booking profile is their entire web presence. Searching the name surfaces same-name salons in New York and Hawaii first.
angle: Their own name doesn't return them in search. That's the demo - run the search in front of them.

name: Illusions Hair Salon
note: Fresha, Yelp and a Groupon deal page - no site of their own. Thirty-seven photos live on Yelp instead.
angle: They're paying Groupon's margin for reach. A site plus their own booking keeps that revenue.

name: Manning Hair Ltd
note: Fresha only, with 73 reviews collected on Birdeye that nothing of theirs links to.
angle: Those 73 reviews are an asset sitting on someone else's page. Put them on a site they own.

name: Burgess & Associates CPA
note: Downtown CPA firm with two Alberta locations and no website. Directories and a BBB profile only.
angle: Highest-ticket prospect on this list. Professional services buyers check for a site before they call.

name: Erle's Auto Repair
note: No website. Appears across eight directory scrapes, none of them theirs.
angle: Eight sites are already publishing their business details, all of them wrong or incomplete. One correct source fixes it.

name: Wheelhouse Garage Ltd
note: No website. A Twitter/X account is the only thing they've ever published.
angle: They were once written up in the Red Deer Advocate. That press has nowhere to point.

name: Q2 Electrical Contractors Ltd
note: Facebook page only. Most competing Red Deer electricians on the same directory page have real sites.
angle: Commercial electrical tenders get screened online. No site reads as a smaller shop than they are.

name: Edwards & Holloway Health & Wellness
note: A JaneApp booking portal and a Facebook page. No website, despite running an attached massage school and actively hiring.
angle: Two audiences - clients and students - with no place to send either. They have payroll, so they have budget.

name: Fritou Chicken
note: Their only 'site' is a foodpages.ca template subdomain. The menu is scattered across MenuPix, Restaurantify and Sluurpy in versions they don't control.
angle: Four different menus online, none current. Wrong prices cost them at the till - that's the hook.

name: Ranch House Restaurant & Bar
note: Facebook plus a Travel Alberta listing. Everything else is aggregator pages built without them.
angle: Travel Alberta already sends them tourist traffic with nowhere to land it.

name: Penhold Automotive Service & Repair
note: Facebook only. Ten minutes south of Red Deer, in the Town of Penhold business directory with no link.
angle: Small-town shop chasing Red Deer drivers. A site is how they show up in the bigger city's searches.

name: Bayside Barber Shop Inc
note: No website. baysidebarbershop.com belongs to a shop in Bay St. Louis, Mississippi - searching their name sends customers to the wrong country.
angle: The obvious domain is gone. Pitch baysidebarbershop.ca and fix the search result in one move.

name: Sass Studio
note: Instagram, Facebook and a Fresha booking page. No website. Two addresses circulating in directories.
angle: Conflicting addresses online is a walk-in problem, not a marketing one. Easiest opener on the list.

name: Prana Wellness
note: Spread across Fresha, MassageBook and Cortico with no site of their own. Three booking systems, none of them a home page.
angle: Three booking links means three places to lose a client. One site, one button.

name: The Beauty Heaven
note: Facebook plus a Setmore booking page. Thirty-five reviews collected on Birdeye. Home-based, listed under two different street addresses.
angle: A Saskatchewan phone number and two addresses make them look temporary. A site makes them look established.

name: The Brow Lounge
note: Facebook and a Linktree. The Linktree is doing the job a home page should do.
angle: A Linktree is the clearest admission on this list that someone needs a real site. Show them the difference.

name: Choice Developments & Renos
note: No website. Listed on Yelp, Foursquare and YellowPages under two different trade categories, with nothing of their own tying them together.
angle: Renovation buyers shortlist by portfolio. With no photos of finished work anywhere, they can only compete on price.

name: Bracha Concrete & Coatings Inc.
note: No website, and searching the company name returns competitors instead - they don't appear anywhere in the results for their own business.
angle: Type their name into Google in front of them. Seven Calgary concrete companies come back and none of them are theirs.

name: Quake Concrete Line Pumping Ltd
note: Their listed site sits on a webs.com free subdomain - a hosting platform that stopped being current well over a decade ago. It doesn't surface in search for the company name.
angle: A free-host subdomain reads as abandoned to a general contractor vetting subs. Move them to their own domain.

name: Skylark Construction Ltd
note: No website. Search their name and you get Skylark Construction in Oregon and Skylark Construction in Kenya before anything Albertan.
angle: Two foreign firms own their name in search. A site at a .ca domain is the whole fix.

name: Rulam Contracting Ltd
note: An Edmonton Construction Association member with no site of its own. What ranks first is a page on edmontondirect.ca that calls itself their "official website" - a directory using their name.
angle: Commercial work comes through the association and Procore. Someone else is currently the official-looking version of them.
links: The directory page ranking as theirs

name: Diogo Concrete Ltd
note: Facebook only. They post concrete finisher jobs through the federal Job Bank because they have nowhere of their own to advertise.
angle: Hiring is their pain right now, not marketing. Sell the careers page and the rest follows.

name: Dig Zach Earthworks Ltd
note: Their web presence is a single page on gr8businesses.com - a microsite on somebody else's domain, which they can't change, rank or own.
angle: They're renting one page from a directory. Owning digzach.ca costs less than they think.

name: Four Timbers Renovations Ltd.
note: They bought fourtimbers.ca and it still serves a "Coming Soon" page. Meanwhile their reviews collect on GuildQuality and Houzz.
angle: The warmest lead here. They already decided they want a site and paid for the domain - someone just never built it.

name: Skill Builders (1996) Ltd
note: Trading since 1996 with a Facebook page, a HomeStars profile and a BBB listing - and no website.
angle: Thirty years of referrals with no online proof. Their HomeStars reviews are the content; they just need somewhere to put them.

name: Timber Ridge Custom Builders
note: A custom home builder with no website at all - only Yelp and scraped directory entries.
angle: Custom builds are the highest-consideration purchase on this page. No portfolio online is the whole problem.

name: Bricon
note: No website. bricon.ca belongs to a Quebec firm and BriCon Inc. to an Idaho one, so their name returns three other companies first.
angle: Three unrelated Bricons outrank them. Pick a domain that pins them to Red Deer.

name: Gold Bond Construction Ltd
note: One YellowPages listing is their entire presence on the internet. Nothing else returns for the company name.
angle: Genuinely invisible online. Anything at all would be an improvement - start small and cheap.

name: Sundance Deck Solutions
note: No website. Search the name and you get Houzz category pages and competing Calgary deck builders - never them.
angle: Decks are bought from photos. Houzz is showing their competitors' galleries on searches that should be theirs.
